Disruption is expected until 10:15.
Customer advice:
If you are travelling between Oxted and East Croydon you can travel on your normal route, but services may be disrupted.
You will need to allow at least an additional 15 minutes to complete your journey.
Please talk to station staff, look at the information boards or check your journey planner for the most recent information.
Please be aware that this may also affect services down to Uckfield and East Grinstead.
Planning your journey:
For help planning your journey, check live departure boards, view a live network map or see alternative route guides.
If you’re travelling within London, you can use the TfL Journey Planner.
Stay up to date on the move with Southern’s WhatsApp channel. Live updates are available Monday to Friday, 07:00–21:00.
Can you tell me more about the incident?
Trains are likely to have some delays due to a fault with a signal in this area. In this case, the signal has been reported to be switching rapidly between different colours and not showing a steady indication to drivers. This means drivers have to stop at the preceding signal and gain verbal instructions to continue. Your journey will unfortunately take longer as a result.
Railway signals are designed to warn drivers that they have to stop because the system can't yet confirm that the route ahead is clear. In most places, the signalling system will show a green light, or aspect, when the track is clear for a long distance ahead, and drivers will then be shown one or two yellow lights to warn them when they are approaching a red signal. This means that they can anticipate the amount of braking that's required to stop before they reach another train or any form of problem on the line. In this case, as the signal isn't reliably showing the necessary indications to drivers, they'll need to take extra safety precautions to travel through the area.
The signalling system is maintained by Network Rail, Southern and Thameslink are working closely with them to diagnose the fault and make sure it is fixed as quickly as possible. Until this is done, they will be closely monitoring the train service and doing their best to keep to the timetable.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.

nrIncident.routes: Between Bognor Regis / Eastbourne / Littlehampton / East Grinstead / Horsham / Ore / Reigate / Dorking / Epsom Downs / Sutton / West Croydon / London Bridge and London Victoria

A fault with the signalling system between Clapham Junction and London Victoria means that some lines are disrupted. As a result, trains running between these stations may be delayed by up to 25 minutes.
This is expected until 12:45.
Customer advice:
If you are travelling between Clapham Junction and London Victoria you can travel on your normal route, but services will be disrupted.
You will need to allow at least an additional 20 minutes to complete your journey.
Please talk to station staff, look at the information boards or check your journey planner for the most recent information.
Planning your journey:
For help planning your journey, check live departure boards, view a live network map or see alternative route guides.
If you’re travelling within London, you can use the TfL Journey Planner.

Can you tell me more about the incident?
Track circuits are part of the signalling system and are used to detect where trains are on the railway. If one fails, the signalling system may show that a section of track is occupied even when there isn’t a train there. This means signals protecting that section will remain at red and trains cannot proceed normally.
Trains may still be able to run, but drivers will need to stop before the affected section and request verbal permission from the signaller before continuing past the red signal. They must then travel at a reduced speed so they can stop safely should they see anything ahead of them.
This takes longer than usual and can cause trains to queue behind one another. In severe cases, services may need to be cancelled, revised or diverted to prevent delays from building up across the wider network."
Network Rail signalling specialists are investigating the fault and will work to repair the affected equipment. Once the fault has been fixed and the signalling system is working normally, trains will be able to run at normal speeds again and the scheduled service can begin to recover.
